question: What does healthcare data access primarily allow authorized medical personnel to do?

options.A: Retrieve, view, and utilize patient information
options.D: Share patient details publicly on social media

explanation: Data access gives clinicians the ability to pull up and use patient records to guide medical care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is rapid access to patient information critical for nurses at the bedside?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal patient handovers
options.B: It eliminates the need for physical patient assessments
options.C: It allows nurses to diagnose surgical conditions alone
options.D: It prevents treatment delays and duplicate testing

explanation: Having quick access to past medical history and test results helps nurses avoid repeating tests and speeds up safe care delivery. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of demographic data found in an EHR?

options.D: Patient home address and phone number

explanation: Demographics refer to basic personal and contact details rather than clinical test results or treatments. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: What part of the health record typically makes up the largest share of daily clinical data inputs?
explanation: Nurses constantly input vital signs, assessment notes, and care updates throughout their shifts, making up the bulk of clinical data. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of legal frameworks like HIPAA regarding patient data?

options.A: To establish boundaries for how health data is protected and shared
options.B: To mandate the specific brand of computers a clinic must purchase
options.C: To ensure all medical textbooks are printed in digital formats
options.D: To dictate how much hospitals can charge for daily room stays

explanation: Privacy laws set strict rules to safeguard patient records from unauthorized viewing and improper disclosure. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h3)

question: A nurse uses the hospital computer to check the medical chart of a famous musician admitted to a different ward, simply out of personal curiosity. What is the legal and ethical status of this action?

options.A: It is allowed if the nurse is off-duty during the chart review
options.B: It is acceptable as long as the nurse does not tell anyone else
options.C: It is a serious privacy breach because the nurse is outside the circle of care
options.D: It is encouraged so staff can offer collective words of encouragement

explanation: Looking at charts without a direct professional need for patient care violates data privacy laws and ethics. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why is sharing your computer login password with a colleague during a busy shift dangerous?

options.A: It locks the computer hardware permanently until IT resets it
options.B: It automatically deletes all patient lab reports in the system
options.C: It slows down the hospital internet connection speed significantly
options.D: It breaks accountability because actions under that login are tied to your name

explanation: Every action in an EHR is logged against the active user account, so sharing credentials destroys reliable audit trails. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which practice helps prevent visual eavesdropping on patient electronic health records in a busy ward?

options.A: Leaving workstation sessions logged in overnight for easy access
options.B: Writing patient passwords on sticky notes attached to the monitor
options.C: Positioning computer screens away from public view and hallways
options.D: Using large font sizes so visitors can read updates from afar

explanation: Shielding monitors from visitors and passersby stops unauthorized people from reading sensitive clinical data on screen. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h4)

question: What does interoperability mean in the context of health information systems?

options.A: All nurses use the exact same brand of computer tablet
options.B: Patients can print their own physical charts at home
options.C: Different software systems can communicate and exchange data smoothly
options.D: Hospital billing software automatically calculates staff salaries

explanation: Interoperability allows separate technology platforms to share information without manual re-entry. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main problem caused by a lack of interoperability between hospital departments?

options.A: Nurses spend less time documenting and more time at the bedside
options.B: Patients are automatically discharged by the computer software
options.C: Computers consume too much electricity and overheat during shifts
options.D: Data gets trapped in silos, leading to manual re-entry and communication delays

explanation: When systems do not connect, clinical details remain isolated, forcing staff to waste time calling or copying data by hand. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h5)

question: What responsibility do nurses hold regarding data integrity in the electronic health record?

options.A: Ensuring accurate and timely data entry to protect patient safety
options.B: Writing the underlying computer code for the hospital software
options.C: Repairing broken hardware terminals in patient rooms
options.D: Setting up new user accounts for incoming hospital doctors

explanation: Nurses must enter correct information carefully because mistakes in the chart can directly harm patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)

question: A patient asks how to view their recent laboratory test results from home. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Guide the patient on how to access their secure online health portal
options.B: Print the entire hospital database and mail it to their home
options.C: Tell the patient that viewing lab results is strictly illegal for laypeople
options.D: Read all hospital lab results out loud over a public phone call

explanation: Nurses empower patients by showing them how to use secure patient portals to check their own health records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is 'click fatigue' in the context of electronic health records?

options.A: Physical hand cramps caused by holding a computer mouse too tightly
options.B: Spending excessive time navigating confusing menus and clicking through screens
options.C: A battery failure in wireless barcode scanners during night shifts
options.D: Eye strain from staring at bright computer monitors all day

explanation: Click fatigue happens when poor software design forces clinicians to perform too many clicks to complete simple documentation tasks. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is a major risk when electronic health record systems experience sudden downtime?

options.A: All medication pumps stop working simultaneously
options.B: Staff must revert to paper charting, which can increase transcription errors
options.C: Hospital doors automatically lock to prevent patient entry
options.D: Patient vital signs automatically delete themselves from memory

explanation: System downtime forces a return to manual paper records, raising the chance of mistakes during handovers and order transcription. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h7)

question: How are wearable health trackers beginning to influence professional health records?

options.A: By replacing the need for licensed nurses in hospital wards
options.B: By serving as the primary billing invoice for insurance companies
options.C: By feeding real-time patient metrics directly into clinical systems
options.D: By automatically prescribing medications without a doctor's order

explanation: Wearables like smartwatches are starting to integrate live patient data such as heart rate and activity into medical records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary benefit of cloud-based health records in modern medical practice?

options.A: They allow secure access to patient charts across multiple clinic sites
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for patient confidentiality laws
options.C: They make physical nurse assessments completely unnecessary
options.D: They prevent patients from ever seeing their own test results

explanation: Cloud storage lets authorized staff retrieve patient records seamlessly from different locations without relying on local hospital servers. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h8)
